title: httpd Module
content_markdown:
This module provides an HTTP transport layer for OpenSIPS.

Implementation of httpd module's http server is based on libmicrohttpd library.

TLS for the http server is enabled by setting the `tls_cert_file` and `tls_key_file` parameters. If this is enabled, support for plain http is disabled.
overview:
This module provides an HTTP transport layer for OpenSIPS.

Implementation of httpd module's http server is based on libmicrohttpd library.

TLS for the http server is enabled by setting the `tls_cert_file` and `tls_key_file` parameters. If this is enabled, support for plain http is disabled.
how_it_works: Due to the fact that OpenSIPS is a multiprocess application, the microhttpd library is used in "external select" mode. This ensures that the library is not running in multithread mode and the library is entirely controled by OpenSIPS. Due to this particular mode of operations, for now, the entire http response is built in a pre-allocated buffer (see buf_size parameter).

dependencies_required.name: libmicrohttpd
dependencies_required.reason: Implementation of httpd module's http server is based on libmicrohttpd library. Must be installed with EPOLL support, typically a version newer than 0.9.50.

exported_parameters.name: ip
exported_parameters.description: The IP address used by the HTTP server to listen for incoming requests.
exported_parameters.notes: The default value is "127.0.0.1" (binds to loopback only). Use "*" to bind to all IPv6 and IPv4 interfaces.

exported_parameters.name: port
exported_parameters.description: The port number used by the HTTP server to listen for incoming requests.
exported_parameters.notes: Ports lower than 1024 are not accepted.

exported_parameters.name: conn_timeout
exported_parameters.description: Auto-close TCP connections which are idle for more than the designated timeout, in seconds. Set to zero to never close any connections.
exported_parameters.notes: Note: the connection auto-close routine only seems to be executed in an "on-demand" fashion, during an HTTPD network event (e.g. on a new connection), which although not ideal, it should be good enough in practical terms.

exported_parameters.name: buf_size
exported_parameters.description: It specifies the maximum length (in bytes) of the buffer used to write in the html response.
exported_parameters.notes: If the size of the buffer is set to zero, it will be automatically set to a quarter of the size of the pkg memory.

exported_parameters.name: post_buf_size
exported_parameters.description: It specifies the length (in bytes) of the POST HTTP requests processing buffer. For large POST request, the default value might require to be increased.

exported_parameters.name: receive_buf_size
exported_parameters.description: It specifies the maximum length (in bytes) of the received HTTP requests. For receiving large POST request, the default value might require to be increased.

exported_parameters.name: tls_cert_file
exported_parameters.description: Public certificate file for httpd. It will be used as server-side certificate for incoming TLS connections.

exported_parameters.name: tls_key_file
exported_parameters.description: Private key of the above certificate. I must be kept in a safe place with tight permissions!

exported_parameters.name: tls_ciphers
exported_parameters.description:
You can specify the list of algorithms for authentication and encryption that you allow. To obtain a list of ciphers and then choose, use the gnutls-cli application:

*   gnutls-cli -l


### Warning

Do not use the NULL algorithms (no encryption) ... never!!!

exported_parameters.name: auth_realm
exported_parameters.description: The realm string to be used for HTTP Basic Authentication challenges. Only takes effect when both `auth_username` and `auth_password` are set.

exported_parameters.name: auth_username
exported_parameters.description: The username for HTTP Basic Authentication. When set together with `auth_password`, all HTTP requests must present valid credentials. Requests without credentials or with incorrect credentials receive a 401 Unauthorized response.

exported_parameters.name: auth_password
exported_parameters.description: The password for HTTP Basic Authentication. Must be set together with `auth_username`.
exported_parameters.notes: When using HTTP Basic Authentication, it is strongly recommended to also enable TLS via `tls_cert_file` and `tls_key_file` to prevent credentials from being transmitted in plaintext.

exported_mi_functions.name: httpd:list_root_path
exported_mi_functions.description:
Replaces obsolete MI command: _httpd\_list\_root\_path_.

Lists all the registered http root paths into the httpd module. When a request comes in, if the root parth is in the list, the request will be sent to the module that register it.
